problem: Embodied Question Answering (EQA) had only been studied in synthetic SUNCG houses with RGB-only perception, where test houses reuse objects seen in training. It was unknown how agents behave in photorealistic scanned homes, and whether 3D (point cloud) perception helps. Behavior cloning of recurrent navigators on long shortest-path trajectories also tends to collapse to 'repeat the previous action'.
motivation: Real robots carry RGB-D sensors and must work in perceptually realistic, unseen homes, so EQA needs a photorealistic benchmark and 3D perception. The authors also observe two problems. First, the standard EQA protocol (agent walked along the shortest path to within 10/30/50 steps of the target) makes naive baselines deceptively strong. Second, teacher-forced cross-entropy rewards copying the previous ground-truth action and misses every transition.
key_idea: Instantiate EQA on Matterport3D (MP3D-EQA) and systematically compare reactive and GRU-memory navigators that perceive via frozen pretrained PointNet++ point-cloud features, ResNet50 RGB features, or both. The navigators are trained by behavior cloning with an 'Inflection Weighting' loss that upweights time steps where the expert action changes.
insight: Inflection weighting is what makes behavior-cloned recurrent navigators learn anything. Without it, NoIW-M and NoIW-M+Q collapse exactly to forward-only (d_T 0.933/1.330 at T-10/T-30, identical to the reactive blind model). With it, M reaches 0.830 at T-30, and M+PC+RGB collision drops from 61.658% to 4.957% at T-10. The evaluation protocol hands control to an agent already roughly facing the target, so forward-only and random are strong. A blind GRU that learns path-shape priors (counting, then turning or stopping) even gets the best d_T at T-10/T-30. Adding vision hurts d_T (reactive models lose the 'functional stop' of crashing into walls; memory models overshoot) but improves IoU_T and lowers collisions. Point clouds give the lowest collision rates (M+PC 9.169% vs M+RGB 15.130% at T-30), RGB gives more semantic signal, and PC+RGB gets the best IoU_T.
method: MP3D-EQA dataset: questions templated from Matterport3D annotations, in three types: location ('What room is the <OBJ> located in?'), color, and color_room. Object colors come from AMT: 24-color palette, 5 votes per object, majority vote. Low-entropy questions are filtered out, and only the (object, room) pair must be unique. Totals: ~1136 questions over 83 homes; train/val/test = 57/10/16 homes and 767/130/239 questions, following the MINOS environment split. Episodes are restricted to a single floor.

Point-cloud simulator: built on MINOS. A global point cloud is fused from the MP3D panoramas; per view, points are frustum-culled, then an occlusion/free-space check against the rasterized mesh depth buffer drops points (tolerance ε=0.25 cm). A sparse-to-dense two-pass visibility check keeps this fast.

PointNet++ encoder: multi-scale-grouping set abstractions (1024/256/64 centroids) plus a global SA giving a 1024-d feature. A learned 32-d 'sparsity embedding' (5 bins over the point count in [0, 2^14]) is concatenated to form a 1056-d observation. The encoder is pretrained on ~100k MP3D frames with three decoders: semantic segmentation (40 classes, FP layers), color autoencoding (smooth-L1) and structure autoencoding (MLP, earth-mover's distance). It is then frozen.

RGB encoder: ResNet50 on 224×224 egocentric frames, jointly pretrained on segmentation (class-weighted CE), depth and autoencoding (smooth-L1), with λ = 0.1/10/10 and 1×1-conv + bilinear decoders. It is then frozen and replaces the shallow CNN of Das et al.

Navigators (PACMAN-style): Reactive (R) is a feed-forward net over the concatenated last 5 observation embeddings. Memory (M) is a 2-layer GRU taking the current observation, previous action and, optionally, a 2-layer 128-d LSTM question encoding; it uses GroupNorm. Actions are forward / turn-left / turn-right / stop. The design is crossed over 4 perception inputs {None, PC, RGB, PC+RGB} × question/no-question, giving 16 models.

Behavior cloning with Inflection Weighting: training uses ~11,796 expert shortest-path episodes (LazyTheta* in continuous space, greedily converted to actions) toward the 'best view', i.e. the view maximizing IoU between the target mask and a fixed centered box. The loss is cross-entropy weighted by w_t = N/n_I (~5.7) where a_t ≠ a_{t-1} (first step counts as an inflection) and 1 otherwise, normalized by Σw_t. Checkpoints are chosen by NMS on validation loss, then end-to-end validation of QA + d_Δ at T-50.

QA module: 'spatial+RGB+Q' uses a bag-of-words question encoder and scaled dot-product spatial attention over the last-frame ResNet feature map, followed by an element-wise product with the question and classification over 53 answers. It is trained with the ground-truth navigator and used to answer for every navigator.

setting.backbone: PointNet++ point-cloud encoder and/or ResNet50 RGB encoder (both pretrained on MP3D auxiliary tasks, frozen) + 2-layer GRU (memory) or MLP (reactive) navigator with LSTM question encoder, trained from scratch by behavior cloning; separate spatial-attention VQA module (ResNet50 + BoW)
setting.training_data: MP3D-EQA train split (57 homes, 767 questions) with ~11,796 shortest-path expert trajectories (~15 per question-environment pair). ~100,000 simulator frames from Matterport3D for perception pretraining (segmentation/color/structure or depth). AMT color annotations collected for MP3D objects.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (224×224) and/or egocentric 2.5D colored point cloud (≤2^14 points, rendered from MP3D aligned scans) + question text; no map, GPS or compass
setting.action_space: discrete forward / turn-left / turn-right / stop (10/30/50 actions ≈ 0.35/1.89/3.54 m)
setting.simulator: custom MINOS-based simulator on Matterport3D (mesh RGB renders + point-cloud renderer)
setting.privileged: EQA protocol of Das et al.: the agent is spawned randomly, then walked along the ground-truth shortest path until it is 10/30/50 actions from the target before being given control (gives a heading prior). The QA module is trained with the ground-truth navigator. No map, pose or semantics are given at test time.

numbers_note: The main paper gives navigation results only in figures (at T-30). All numeric results come from the supplementary full tables, for inflection-weighted and NoIW models. The supplementary CI table captioned as the inflection-weighted results with CIs carries 'NoIW-' row labels, but its values match the inflection-weighted table: an apparent labeling error. There is no explicit Fwd row; the blind reactive models R/R+Q learned forward-only. QA numbers in the navigation tables all use the spatial+RGB+Q answerer and are printed as fractions (e.g. 0.411), converted here to percent. Only the rows with inflection weighting, which is the default, are recorded here.
results: No learned navigator dominates on MP3D-EQA test. With inflection weighting, the blind memory navigator M gets the best d_T at T-10/T-30 (0.366/0.830 vs forward-only 0.933/1.330 and Random 0.912/1.273), and M+PC+RGB gets the best d_T at T-50 (1.791) and the best IoU_T (0.209/0.179 at T-10/T-30 vs 0.062/0.050 for forward-only). Point-cloud models collide least (M+PC 9.169% vs M+RGB 15.130% at T-30). QA gains over blind baselines are small: best end-to-end 41.1% (M+PC at T-30) vs 37.9% for forward-only and 45.1% with the shortest-path oracle. The best answerer reaches 46.2% on val with the ground-truth navigator vs 38.3% for a BoW question-only model.
limitations: Behavior cloning from a shortest-path expert never shows mistakes or exploration, so navigators barely use the question (color_room info) and cannot recover from errors; no RL fine-tuning is done.

The inherited EQA evaluation protocol (walking the agent along the shortest path before handing control) makes forward-only and random baselines hard to beat, and vision hurts distance metrics. End-to-end QA barely exceeds question-only baselines, because the VQA models are naive.
Small dataset (~1136 templated questions, 3 types). Relies on imperfect MP3D mesh/point-cloud reconstructions; simulation only, no real-robot validation.
